description.narrative: This project is supported by the climate justice work in FAIR FOR ALL. FAIR for ALL objectives are to contribute to a world in which global value chains serve people and planet before profit. People before profit is the global slogan of Fridays for Future (FFF)and this project is to support the MAPA (Most Affected People and Areas) collective within Fridays for Future. This grant, collaboration and support aims to strengthen this important movement and reference point for our global and national climate and food security work. Fridays For Future MAPA helps to hold governments and private sector to account and mobilises young people all across the world as part of their Climate Strikes which Oxfam Novib has been a supporter of for many years. As well as our work to better engage young people in meaningful ways. Through this grant we supporting youth-led feminist and decolonial movement. We do this via theirfiscal host Climate 2025 both who we have worked with around COP27. A strong diverse climate movement that centres the voices, experiences, ideas and solutions of those least responsible yet most impacted by the climate crises, is part of our climate justice objectives. This grant will contribute to strengthening an important part of that climate movement - Fridays for Future Most Affected People’s and Areas (MAPA) collective. Provide seed money to FFF MAPA via their fiscal host Climate 2025 to do the first phase of theirprocess to reflect, re-organise and re-strategise; use the grant to access guidance and support on strengthening their movement andas part of that develop a proposal for funders to finance and support an eventual face to face strategizing meeting for their collective that is an important part of the broader FFF movement.

participating-org.narrative:
Since Climate 2025 was founded in April 2020, we have grown our team, expanded our offerings, served more and more movements, and learnt a lot. Through all this, our core mission has not changed: activating and amplifying an ecosystem of movements working for urgent systemic change in response to the climate and ecological emergency. The geopolitical landscape has shifted at an alarming rate in many countries towards fascism, yet devastatingly slow to embed and enforce realistic environmental policies and regulations across the globe. There has never been more need for citizen engagement: to stand up courageously against corruption and poor leadership. 2021 saw flaccid ambition at COP26 in Glasgow, continued suffering for those most affected, and the realisation of past scientificpredictions: our unstable climate has intensified extreme weather events causing chaos within communities and crop productions. A surge of youth-led activism has kept our optimism resolute, and we are honoured to work in this space, providing movements with the support they need, to achieve the impact that is essential for humanity to survive.
At Climate 2025, we provide infrastructure and capacity-building support to high-potential emerging movements.
Climate 2025 offers: 1. Capacity Building 2. Access to Funding 3. Fiscal hosting 4. Ecosystem mapping 5. Stakeholder Engagement
Each of these programmes work in tandem, enabling us to refresh the movement ecosystem by amplifying new ideas and faces, activate movements through fiscal hosting, access to funding and capacity building, and, amplify movements through ecosystem mapping and stakeholder engagement.
